# MobyGames — critic and player review index

- Source: [MobyGames — Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood reviews](https://www.mobygames.com/game/7907/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/reviews/)
- Archived copy: [Wayback Machine, 2024-12-08](https://web.archive.org/web/20241208020314/https://www.mobygames.com/game/7907/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood/reviews/)
- The supplied HTML was gzip-compressed and was decompressed in memory. The companion `.txt` is only a decoding warning, not proof the page is missing.
- The page reports 37 critic ratings (average 81%), a MobyGames score of 7.9/10, and one player review among 20 ratings (average 3.9/5).

## English translation

Complete translations of the non-English excerpts follow; originals are retained below.

For English-language records, the source wording itself is the complete English translation. They are included here in the source order, with foreign-language records translated at the corresponding point.

### Game Chronicles (English; 2002-11-28; Windows; 94/100)

Robin Hood mixes up a great blend of ambush, spy, infiltration, and strategic missions to create a wonderful campaign package. The puzzles are integrated seamlessly into a rich and living world that is visually spectacular with a story that is true to the legend of Robin Hood. The intuitive control system keeps the challenge within the gameplay and not the interface.

### Fragland.net (English; 2002-12-17; Windows; 88/100)

In conclusion I would like to say that Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is a very enjoyable game which will keep you amused for hours on end ! As I said, the colouring and the artwork is simply amazing, it's a feast to look at !! I'm glad I had the chance to play (and review :) this game. Perhaps you should rewrite that letter to Santa Claus :)

### GameSpy (English; 2003-02; Windows; 87/100)

Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood turned out to be a pleasant surprise. It combines clever missions, interesting character abilities, and a smidgen of resource management into an absorbing game that fans of the strategy will be playing for quite some time.

### ActionTrip (English; 2002-12-05; Windows; 87/100)

The only noteworthy downside to the game is that once you've finished it, you will have little on no desire to play it again, which goes hand in hand with the lack of the multiplayer mode. In other words, the replay value of Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is extremely low. But can this be measured with a great authentic feeling of being the most righteous thief in human history? I think not. My recommendation is that fans of tactical strategy games go out and buy this one. The gameplay is well thought-out, and the game design concepts are excellently executed.

### Armchair Empire (English; 2002-11-25; Windows; 86/100)

Probably one of the most underrated RTS games last year was Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive. It had a huge amount of challenge and it did justice to the Wild West setting with some slick graphics and sound. Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood (LoS) does the same thing for the Sherwood Forest while sticking closely to the conventions of Desperados, which is a good thing and a bad thing.

### Worth Playing (English; 2002-12-16; Windows; 86/100)

Overall, Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is a pretty good game. Not everyone is going to like it, especially impatient people due to the fact tactics aren’t usually planned and performed at the drop of a hat, or people who expect an easy game, but anyone who likes tactical games or is interested in the legend of Robin Hood will more than likely enjoy the game. The difficulty level is configurable, so those who do have a tough time will be able to tone it down a bit, but there will still be some who will have a hard time.

### GameSpot (English; 2002-11-12; Windows; 86/100)

Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood's romantic depiction of Robin and his Merry Men and its clever game design really help bring the swashbuckling legend to life, much like the classic Errol Flynn movie. It's a bit of a shame that the game is so lacking in the way of extras, such as multiplayer options or an editor of any kind, but the campaign itself is presented extremely well. Games such as these, which are based on classic themes or stories, often tend to fall short of the mark, but Robin Hood gets its subject matter right, and with plenty of playability, storytelling, and atmosphere.

### Daily PC Game Reviews (English; 2011-02-27; Windows; 85/100)

With 16 huge levels for you to complete and a continuous supply of ambush missions, I'd say that there is great replayability in Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood. There are many ways to skin a cat, so there are also many ways you can achieve victory for every mission. Moreover, you have three difficulty levels to choose from if you find it too simple on Easy level. Already, I find the game to be as difficult as Commandos and cannot fathom why you might want a harder challenge. Well, the option is there for hardcore players who love challenges.

I suggest you get Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood today, so that you can relive the days of yore where an arrow from a talented archer can help save the day for the destitute, unfortunate, and oppressed.

So do you fancy stealing from the rich, and giving to the poor? Anytime for me, please.

### GameZone (English; 2002-11-11; Windows; 85/100)

Robin Hood – The Legend of Sherwood is well done, and quite enjoyable. The missions get harder as you progress, and players will be asked to use their brains rather than just blindly wading into battle. Fans of the era, fans of Robin Hood, and fans of tactical combat games will find this game worth notching their bows for.

### IGN (English; 2002-11-21; Windows; 82/100)

Overall, I was happily surprised with Robin Hood. Well, maybe not surprised so much since I enjoyed Spellbound's Desperados, but the new features such as resource management and the non-linear mission path is a great addition to the genre. These new hooks will be sorely missed if they're not included in future games of this type, and Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is responsible for starting them.

### Computer Gaming World (CGW) (English; 2003-03; Windows; 80/100)

Its tough to find much to fault. It is possible to lose track of characters behind tall buildings, and it would have been fantastic to have a multiplayer cooperative mode. But these are minor issues, and I can highly recommend Robin Hood to anyone who enjoys devilishly clever plans and swashbuckling adventure.

### ComputerGames.ro (English; 2003-01-14; Windows; 80/100)

If I have to describe Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood with just one word I'd say it's nice. Even if you won't play it again, unless you want to test another difficulty level and this is hard to believe also, the game is made to be consumed during the morning when you're having a hot cup of coffee or tea or just to keep your girlfriend from hurting your GeForce with a Solitaire in the evening when she thinks your computer is all hers. Basically, it will fill your spare time and it will stay installed for some time. On my computer it stayed for about 20 hours or less and I didn't hurry to finish the missions so I guess you got the point. Enjoy!

### CanadianGamer (English; 2003-03-21; Windows; 80/100)

Overall, Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is a very unique game that combines elements of several genres. Some adventuring, role-playing, strategic manoeuvres, and some resource management are all part of this package. It is also very nice to see familiar characters such as Friar Tuck and Little John. Leading them against evil Prince John will make many people satisfied. If you've enjoyed similar games (Commandos and Desperados are good examples), or are looking for a unique game with a fresh setting, this game will offer you a pleasant gaming experience.

### Appletell (English; 2011-10-21; Macintosh; 60/100)

All that aside, Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is a solid game. I’m glad to see it revived, but it wasn’t perfect in 2005, and hardly anything has been corrected. It gets repetitious, but the story is often enough to pull you through to the next level. Fans of Robin Hood will be pleased. Fans of strategy games in general? Well, it depends upon how retro you’re willing to go.

### Macworld (English; 2005-04-15; Macintosh; 60/100)

Though it might not hold a visual candle to more sophisticated fare and is lacking in the replay department, Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood will appeal to users of older Macs looking for some fun strategy gaming.

### CyberMycha (Polish; 2003-03; Windows; 100/100)

I simply have to say it. Robin Hood: Legend of Sherwood restored my faith in computer games. I have not spent such carefree hours in a long time. The gorgeous graphics catch the eye; I admired every detail, and the appearance and animation of the forest streams made me sentimentally glance at the somewhat dusty fishing rod standing in the corner. The game is easy but enjoyable—that is what games are about: pleasant free time! Simple mouse-click controls are a huge advantage. We look at beautiful landscapes, click on our cheerful group and opponents, look again, click again and suddenly many hours have passed. I really recommend it!

### GameStar (Germany) (German; 2002-11; Windows; 86/100)

The developers have done the non-linear campaign very well. By choosing my next deployment location on the overview map, I at least have a perfect illusion of freedom—even though the story follows its predetermined course. The simple combat system saves me many a sweaty moment that the often stressful *Commandos 2* caused. I easily lose track of time in Sherwood Forest, puzzle over ways to solve things and then throw them out because a brawl with the guards has interrupted my group. This creates many tense moments despite the predictable story. Nevertheless *Robin Hood* cannot overtake *Desperados*, especially because the supporting characters partly have the same talents as the heroes. Still, you can get your cassettes of Irish folk songs ready, because the trip into Sherwood Forest is a must for all tactics fans.

### Bonusweb (Czech; 2002-11-18; Windows; 86/100)

A splendid *Commandos* clone that lacks only more modes and a longer playing time.

### 4Players.de / 4P (German; 2002-11-12; Windows; 85/100)

Spellbound has captured the flair of the good old Robin Hood films superbly and, after *Desperados*, once again presents real-time tactics at a high level. Not only the story, humor and lifelike animated characters create atmosphere, but above all the picturesque medieval setting. The expansive castle complexes and dreamy forests fully exploit the possibilities of two-dimensional graphics. Added to this are varied assignments, impressive AI reactions and tactical possibilities that guarantee many hours of fun. Nevertheless there are small drops of bitterness: there is no continuous narrator, some texts are not read aloud and many resident sounds repeat too quickly. Beginners will also miss a tutorial and have to overcome some frustrating moments because the level design does not tolerate major mistakes.

### Obligement (French; 2006-12; Windows; 85/100)

Spellbound Studios deserves applause for this polished game. Its mixture of tactics and action in non-linear missions avoids excessive repetition. Beautiful graphics and rich sound make it pleasant. The current port sometimes crashes, frustratingly, because the game itself has no real flaw. A patch would be welcome.

### GamesWEB (Slovak; 2003-04-15; Windows; 85/100)

I have a good impression of *Robin Hood*: it is entertaining and easy to play. I can only recommend it. If you want to “hunt” English soldiers and have great fun, do not hesitate; *Robin Hood* is made for it.

### Sector (Slovak; 2002-11-21; Windows; 85/100)

An interesting improvement is the Sherwood headquarters, where you return after each mission and your band produces what you need. You can strategically plan which supplies to replenish or train your people. There are 40 missions, sadly in only eight locations, but difficulty, focus and objectives vary; times vary too, with attacks at night, in foggy mornings, or by day when most people are present.

### Gamesmania.de (German; 2002-11-15; Windows; 85/100)

*Robin Hood* has the certain something that keeps a player at the screen for hours. I liked the robbers’ camp; it is a successful extension of *Desperados*. Sadly the characters lack the Wild West coolness. Better presentation and a contemporary engine could have earned more points, but *Robin Hood* is a must-buy for tacticians and currently has no alternative.

### Games4Mac (German; 2005; Macintosh; 84/100)

*Robin Hood* is surprisingly fun. Apart from bugs, *Legend of Sherwood* can be a pleasant pastime. A more informative printed manual, instead of the English section of the Quickstart Reference, would have been desirable.

### Computer Bild Spiele (German; 2002-11; Windows; 83.4/100)

The good impression is rounded off by fitting medieval but modernly interpreted music. Since the story is right and set in a beautifully drawn environment, this “good” game is a real bull’s-eye.

### PC Games (Germany) (German; 2002-11; Windows; 82/100)

Knocking down and tying up hundreds of soldiers while ensuring nobody is missed is surprisingly fun. Controls are easy and the overview remains clear. *Commandos* veterans should beware: little of its strategic approach remains. You fight a way to the goal without long planning; avoiding contact is not useful. Fun comes from coordinating fighters and binders on many fronts and sending a healer to wounded heroes.

### GamesPort (Czech; 2003-10-04; Windows; 80/100)

Although initially too straightforward and almost uninnovative, I eventually got into it and enjoyed it. Some missions are too few and could be better designed; there could be fewer, more distinct characters. Resource mining is a major, unusual plus. Until *Commandos 3*, you cannot buy a better game.

### Doupe.cz (Czech; 2003-02-21; Windows; 80/100)

A quality *Commandos* offshoot for anyone who finds that genre founder too slow and tactical.

### Games.cz (Czech; 2002-12-06; Windows; 80/100)

An perhaps overly action-oriented *Commandos* clone built around the attractive Robin Hood legend. Several innovations work, but it lacks something extra compared with *Desperados*.

### PC Action (Germany) (German; 2002-11; Windows; 79/100)

You rarely need considered strategies; clubbing is easier. Scenery, voice acting, music and atmosphere are strengths. There are no major gameplay or graphics improvements over *Desperados*, though no club-swinging supermen trivialize the game. Spellbound recognized the balancing problem and planned an update; ideally it would increase fun by around 5%.

### GameSpot (Belgium/Netherlands) (Dutch; 2003-01-25; Windows; 78/100)

Enemy AI is at least challenging; impressive hand-painted graphics complete the game. Sound is remarkably good and creates a wonderful atmosphere. The story is “captivating,” making the game worth seeing.

### Gameplay (Benelux) (Dutch; 2002-11-30; Windows; 78/100)

*Robin Hood* is a fun game that builds on existing formulas but suffers from a lack of variety…

### PC Zone Benelux (Dutch; 2003-01; Windows; 77/100)

The engine brings Robin Hood’s world to life without making a great impression. Levels look nice from a distance but become unpleasantly blocky when zoomed. Day/night changes, water reflections and fog are present, but nothing revolutionary. Sound is better, especially the background music, which fits the atmosphere perfectly.

### Hry Sme (Slovak; 2003-04-25; Windows; 70/100)

If you like this type of game, there is nothing to discuss. At the highest difficulty it is a successful *Commandos* variation lasting a long time. For undemanding entertainment without using your head, I do not recommend it; you would not last long in Sherwood.

### GamesWEB (Czech; 2003-01-28; Windows; 70/100)

Since the authors used *Commandos* as their example for *Desperados*, they could at least have used *Commandos 2* as their example for *Robin Hood*.

### Clubic (French; 2002-12-06; Windows; 70/100)

A known concept little exploited by current games, flawless implementation on modest systems and adequate length let *Robin Hood* stand out. That is already a fine achievement; being as enjoyable for beginners as experts means one would have to be churlish not to applaud Spellbound.

### Jeuxvideo.com (French; 2002-11-22; Windows; 60/100)

Good ideas are undermined by levels demanding force rather than a genuine *Commandos*-style puzzle. Combat seems designed for this, with favorable skirmishes even one against five. Between action and tactics, Spellbound’s game struggles to find its place, though its innovations are appealing.

### Joystick (France) (French; 2002-11; Windows; 60/100)

It tastes and smells like *Desperados*, but is less successful. Combat replaces thought; too often soldiers can simply be eliminated one by one with sword or bow, without subtle diversion tactics. It is for action/tactics die-hards; newcomers should choose cheap *Desperados* or *Commandos 2*.

### Critic reviews

The following preserves every critic citation shown by the page (source, date, platform and score).

**CyberMycha** — 2003-03 — Windows — 6/6 (100/100) [Polish]

> Po prostu muszę to powiedzieć. Robin Hood: Legenda Sherwood przywrócił mi wiarę w gry komputerowe. Dawno nie spędziłem tak beztroskich godzin, jak podczas zabawy z tą grą. Prześliczna grafika przyciągałą oko; zachwycałem się każdym szczegółem, a wygląd i animacja leśnych potokó spowodowały, że z rozrzewieniem zerknąłem na stojącą w kącie, nieco już zakurzoną wędkę. Do tego wszystkiego, sama gra jest łątwa, lecz przyjemna - i o to w grach chodzi: o miłe spędzenie wolnego czasu! Prosta obsługa, sprowadzająca się głównie do nieskomplikowanego klikania myszką, jest tu ogromną zaletą. Tak sobie siedzimy przed monitorem, oglądamy piękne krajobrazy, klikamy na naszą wesołą gromadkę, klikamy na przeciwników, znowu oglądamy, znowu klikamy i... raptem okazuje się, że minęło sporo godzin! Zatem: naprawdę polecam!

**GameStar (Germany)** — 2002-11 — Windows — 86/100 [German]
> Die nicht-lineare Kampagne ist den Entwicklern sehr gut gelungen. Durch die Auswahl meines nächsten Einsatzortes auf der Übersichtskarte habe ich zumindest eine perfekte Illusion von Freiheit – auch wenn die Story ihren vorgefertigten Lauf nimmt. Das einfache Kampfsystem spart mir so manchen Schweißausbruch, den mir das oft stressige *Commandos 2* bescherte. Leicht vergesse ich im Sherwood Forest die Zeit, knoble an Lösungswegen und werfe sie über den Haufen, weil meiner Gruppe eine Schlägerei mit den Wachen dazwischengekommen ist. So entstehen trotz der berechenbaren Story viele Spannungsmomente. Trotzdem kann Robin Hood *Desperados* nicht überholen, vor allem weil die Nebendarsteller teilweise die gleichen Talente haben wie die Heroen. Dennoch können Sie schon einmal Kassetten mit Irish-Folk-Liedern bereitlegen, denn der Trip in den Sherwood Forest ist ein Muss für alle Taktik-Fans.

**GameSpot** — 2002-11-12 — Windows — 86/100

It's a bit of a shame that the game is so lacking in the way of extras, such as multiplayer options or an editor of any kind, but the campaign itself is presented extremely well. **4Players.de / 4P** — 2002-11-12 — Windows — 85/100 [German]
> Spellbound hat das Flair der guten alten Robin Hood-Verfilmungen hervorragend eingefangen und präsentiert nach Desperados erneut Echtzeit-Taktik auf hohem Niveau. Nicht nur die Story, der Humor und die lebensecht animierten Charaktere sorgen für Atmosphäre, sondern vor allem die malerische Mittelalter-Kulisse. Die weitläufigen Burganlagen und verträumten Wälder reizen die Möglichkeiten zweidimensionaler Grafik voll aus. Hinzu kommen abwechslungsreiche Aufträge, eindrucksvolle KI-Reaktionen und taktische Möglichkeiten, die viele Stunden Spielspaß garantieren. Trotzdem bleiben kleine Wermutstropfen: Es gibt keine durchgehende Erzählerstimme, manche Texte werden nicht vorgelesen und viele Bewohnersounds wiederholen sich zu schnell. Einsteiger werden zudem ein Tutorial vermissen und einige Frustmomente überwinden müssen, weil das Leveldesign keine großen Fehler toleriert.

**Obligement** — 2006-12 — Windows — 85/100 [French]
> On ne peut qu'applaudir Spellbound Studios pour ce jeu bien finiolé. Ce mélange de tactique et d'action dans des missions non-linéaires évite à Robin Hood d'être trop répétitif. Les beaux graphismes rendent le jeu vraiment agréable tout comme l'ambiance sonore riche. Le portage actuel de Robin Hood La Légende De Sherwood plante parfois et c'est rageant car le jeu en lui-même n'a pas vraiment de défaut. Un correctif serait le bienvenu...

**GamesWEB** — 2003-04-15 — Windows — 85/100 [Slovak]
> Z Robina Hooda mám dobrý dojem, ide o zábavnu hru s jednoduchou hratelnosťou. Nič iné mi nezostáva, len aby som vám Robina Hooda odporučil. Takže ak si chcete „zaloviť“ na anglických vojakov, výborne sa zabaviť, neváhajte, Robin Hood je na to ako ušitý.

**Sector** — 2002-11-21 — Windows — 85/100 [Slovak]
> Aby som však nespomínal len negatíva zaujmvaým vylepšením je Sherwoodska centrála kam sa vraciate po každej misií a kde vám vaša banda vyrába všetko čo by ste mohli potrebovať. Môžete si aspoň trochu strategicky naplánovať ktoré zásoby chcete doplniť, alebo či chcete radšej potrénovať svojich ľudí. Máte tú 40 rôznych misií síce škoda že len na 8 rôznych lokáciách, ale dosť sa v nich mení obtiažnosť, zameranie a aj cieľ. Takisto aj čas býva rôzny a niekedy budete útočiť v noci, ráno za hmly, alebo cez deň keď je tam najviac ľudí.

**Gamesmania.de** — 2002-11-15 — Windows — 85/100 [German]
> Robin Hood hat das Gewisse Etwas, das einen Spieler stundenlang vor die Mattscheibe fesselt und ihn das Geschen um ihn herum vergessen lässt. Die Idee mit dem Räuberlager hat mir gefallen, insgesamt eine gelungene Erweiterung des Spielkonzepts von Desperados. Schade nur, dass die Charaktere nicht wieder eine solche Coolness wie im Wilden Westen ausstrahlen. Mit einer etwas besseren Präsentation und einer zeitgemäßen Grafik-Engine hätten noch ein paar Punkte mehr dringesessen. Aber genug der Meckerei: Robin Hood ist Pflichtkauf für Taktiker, eine Alternative gibt es derzeit nicht.

**Games4Mac** — 2005 — Macintosh — 84/100 [German]
> Robin Hood ist ein überraschend spaßiges Spiel. Sieht man von den verschiedenen Bugs im Spiel einmal ab, so kann Robin Hood - Legende von Sherwood ein netter Zeitvertreib sein. Ein etwas informativeres gedrucktes Handbuch anstelle des Englischsprachigen Teil der Quickstart Referenz wäre dennoch wünschenswert gewesen.

**Computer Bild Spiele** — 2002-11 — Windows — 83.4/100 [German]
> Der gute Eindruck wird durch passende mittelalterliche, aber modern interpretierte Musik abgerundet. Da auch die Geschichte stimmt und in einer wunderschön gezeichneten Umgebung spielt, ist dieses „gute“ Spiel ein echter Volltreffer.

**PC Games (Germany)** — 2002-11 — Windows — 82/100 [German]
> Hunderte Soldaten niederschlagen und fesseln, dabei peinlichst genau darauf achten, dass man niemanden übersieht - man mag es kaum glauben, aber das macht richtig Spaß. Die Bedienung geht erfreulich leicht von der Hund und der Überblick bleibt stets gewahrt. Commandos-Recken seien allerdings gewarnt: Von dem strategischen Vorgehen des Vorbilds blieb in Robin Hood nur wenig übrig. Hier wird ohne lange Vorausplanung ein Weg zum Ziel freigekämpft; die in Commandos übliche Vermeidung des Feindkontakts ist im Desperados-Nachfolger nicht sinnvoll. Der Spielspaß entsteht stattdessen dadurch, dass man die Kämpfer und Fessel-Experten an zahlreichen Fronten gleichzeitig koordinieren und gelegentlich einen Heiler zu den verletzten Recken dirigieren muss.

**IGN** — 2002-11-21 — Windows — 82/100
> Overall, I was happily surprised with Robin Hood. Well, maybe not surprised so much since I enjoyed Spellbound's Desperados, but the new features such as resource management and the non-linear mission path is a great addition to the genre. These new hooks will be sorely missed if they're not included in future games of this type, and Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood is responsible for starting them.

**GamesPort** — 2003-10-04 — Windows — 80/100 [Czech]
> Ačkoliv mě tato hra ze začátku vůbec nechytla a jevila se až moc přímočarou a skoro neinovativní, tak jsem se po delší době celkem do hry vžil a docela mě i pobavila. Mám však výtky k designu některých misí, kterých není zrovna mnoho a mohly být o dost lépe udělané. Dále je to k charakterům, kterých mohlo být méně, ale více rozdílných. Velké plus hry je možnost těžení surovin, které je u těchto typů her skutečně nezvyklé. Dokud tedy nevyjde Commandos 3, nemůžete si koupit lepší hru, než je právě tato.

Basically, it will fill your spare time and it will stay installed for some time. Leading them against evil Prince John will make many people satisfied. Tot slot is het verhaal van het type 'meeslepend', wat van Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood een spel maakt dat mag gezien worden

### Player review

**“Great Historical game, kind of struggling.”** — Andrew Shepard — Windows — 2005 (4.2/5)

**The Good** — This game is part of my favorite genre Medieval/Fantasy or Historical. I decided to buy a small copy of it since it was just $5.00. I like to fight as Robin against those guards of Prince John, and the technique of the bows is easy and fun to shoot with.

**The Bad** — The only thing I don't like about the game is how long it takes to just fight off the guards in sword fighting, it does'nt matter witch mouse button you press they both attack the same.

**The Bottom Line** — You love the medieval ages and love good 3D graphics, you may love this game.
